---
title: Custom components
description: Reuse builtin components as a server-side composite, or ship your own browser component, with defineComponent.
contentType: how-to
---

`defineComponent` creates a component that your pages can use. A component has exactly one of two forms: a server-side composite built from builtin components, or a browser component that you implement in React. Pass `render` for a composite or `path` for a browser component, never both.

## Reuse builtin components in a composite

A composite is a function that returns builtin components. DSUI runs it on the server, so no browser code is involved. Use it for chrome that your pages repeat, such as a status card or a detail header.

```ts
import {
  Card,
  type CardNode,
  defineComponent,
  Value,
} from "@northgraindata/dsui-adapter-sdk";
import { status } from "./resources/status";

export const StatusCard = defineComponent<{ title?: string }, CardNode>({
  id: "status-card",
  render: ({ title }) =>
    Card({ title, content: Value({ source: status(), field: "url" }) }),
});
```

Use it like any builtin component: `StatusCard({ title: "Service" })`.

## Ship a browser component

Use a browser component when no builtin component draws what you need. You declare it on the server, and DSUI loads its implementation in the browser.

<Steps>
<Step>

### Declare the component

Give the component an `id` that starts with your adapter's ID, and point `path` at the module that implements it. Add a Zod schema in `props` so DSUI rejects bad props when it builds the page.

```ts
import { defineComponent, z } from "@northgraindata/dsui-adapter-sdk";

export const Greeting = defineComponent<{ name: string }>({
  id: "my-adapter/greeting",
  path: "./greeting-view.tsx",
  props: z.object({ name: z.string() }),
});
```

Calling `Greeting({ name: "Ada" })` returns a `custom` node. Its props must be JSON, so a component never carries React, HTML, or CSS across the server boundary. An action that you pass in a prop reaches the browser as an action reference.

</Step>
<Step>

### Implement the component

The component receives `client`, `node`, and the helpers for rendering child nodes. Read your props with `componentProps`:

```tsx
import {
  type ComponentProps,
  componentProps,
} from "@northgraindata/dsui-adapter-sdk";

export default function Greeting({ node }: ComponentProps) {
  const props = componentProps<{ name: string }>(node);
  return <p>Hello, {props?.name}</p>;
}
```

The `client` offers `executeResource`, `executeAction`, and `navigate`. Some hosts also provide `watchResource`, `openOverlay`, `closeOverlay`, and `notifyInteraction`, so check that they exist before you call them.

</Step>
<Step>

### Register it in the browser entry

Create one browser entry that maps each component `id` to its implementation. DSUI passes its own copy of React, so your bundle doesn't ship one.

```ts
import Greeting from "./greeting-view";

export function createComponents(React: typeof import("react")) {
  return {
    "my-adapter/greeting": (props: Record<string, unknown>) =>
      React.createElement(Greeting as never, props as never),
  };
}
```

DSUI also passes React DOM and its shared controls. Take controls from this third argument, and import only their types. A control you import would bring a second copy of React into your bundle, and React fails when a page has two.

```ts
import type { UiKit } from "@northgraindata/dsui-adapter-sdk";

export function createComponents(
  React: typeof import("react"),
  _ReactDOM: unknown,
  ui: UiKit,
) {
  return {
    "my-adapter/engine": () =>
      React.createElement(ui.Select, {
        ariaLabel: "Engine",
        options: [{ value: "duckdb", label: "DuckDB" }],
      }),
  };
}
```

`ui` holds `Select`. Its `variant` is `"default"` or `"ghost"`, and its `size` is `"default"` or `"small"`.

Point to the entry from `package.json`:

```json
{
  "dsui": {
    "browser": "./src/browser.ts"
  }
}
```

</Step>
</Steps>

The build fails and names the component when a declared `path` component has no entry in the browser map. Without that check, the page would show "Unknown component" and nothing else would fail.

Server composites run from your adapter's source. Browser components load from the adapter's browser bundle, which DSUI builds along with the adapter.
